correct_recommendations: Pass the checkout connection into hold_seats, so that one checkout uses one connection and the seat hold runs inside the order transaction.
invalid_options: Raise max_size of the pool as the fix, because the same deadlock returns when concurrent checkouts per pod reach the new max_size.
Raise max_connections on Postgres, because the database was at 38 of 200.
Add more checkout-api pods as the fix.
root_cause: checkout holds one pool connection for its transaction and then calls hold_seats, which asks the same pool for a second connection. The pool holds 10 connections per pod. When 10 or more checkouts run at once on one pod, all 10 connections belong to checkouts that each wait for a second one, nobody releases, and every waiter fails with PoolTimeout after 30 s.

dependent_facts.true_value: psycopg_pool ConnectionPool max_size 10, timeout 30 s, per process
checkout holds a connection inside a transaction while hold_seats takes a second connection from the same pool
4 checkout-api pods with one uvicorn process each, so one pool of 10 per pod
in_flight 14, pool_in_use 10, pool_waiting 14 on checkout-api-2; PoolTimeout after 30 s, 10 in hold_seats and 4 in checkout; all 14 return 500
about 3 checkouts in flight per pod, below the pool size
hold_seats commits on its own connection, outside the order transaction

required_questions.question: Why does it only fail under load?
required_questions.expected_answer: Each checkout needs two connections at once. Below 10 concurrent checkouts per pod a second connection is free; at 10 or more, all are held by checkouts that wait for a second one.

required_questions.question: Why does everything fail at once after 30 s?
required_questions.expected_answer: The pool timeout is 30 s; every waiter times out together and the transactions roll back.

required_questions.question: Why not a bigger pool?
required_questions.expected_answer: The deadlock returns when concurrent checkouts reach the new size; on-sale traffic has no upper bound.

valid_alternatives.option: Cap concurrent checkouts per pod below half the pool size, for example a semaphore of 5
valid_alternatives.trade_off: No change to the seat code, but it halves checkout throughput per pod and keeps the seat hold outside the order transaction.
valid_alternatives.primary_when: The seat code cannot change before the next on-sale.

closing_decision: One decision: approve passing the checkout connection into hold_seats, or a single follow-up on it.

understanding.problem: Each checkout holds one pool connection and waits for a second one from the same pool of 10.
understanding.breaks: With 10 or more concurrent checkouts on a pod, every connection is held by a waiter, so all checkouts stall for 30 s and fail together with PoolTimeout.
understanding.fix: Reuse the checkout connection in hold_seats.
understanding.cost: A signature change of hold_seats and its call site.
